Cows pass beta-carotene from grass into their milk, which gives Guernsey milk its golden color. Buffalo turn it into vitamin A instead, so their milk and butter stay bright white.

Our sheep get no grain. They graze a fresh plot of grass twice a day in season, with free-choice hay and natural minerals; a small amount of alfalfa pellets just brings them into the barn for milking. In winter they eat alfalfa hay.

Sheep are seasonal. Most milk comes in spring, while most of you want it in fall, so we freeze milk in late June, within 24 hours of milking at below 0°F with forced air, so it thaws with hardly any flakes.
The lambs stay with their mothers. Milk is tested monthly by DHIA, for pathogens once a year, and our water twice a year. Questions, ideas or complaints? Tell us. If you're happy, tell others!

Camel milk, diabetes and autism

Camel milk is naturally high in insulin-like proteins, and some members with diabetes like to include it in their diet. Diabetics who add camel milk to their diet may find they need less insulin, but that is at their own discretion: any change to insulin or medication should be made together with their doctor. It has also been studied for autism: Dr. Millie Hinkle of North Carolina was one of the first doctors in recent times to study camel milk with autism patients, before Dr. Yagil of Israel, and her research is ongoing.

products.name: Beef Bulgogi
products.desc: Thin slices of beef in a sweet-savory Korean marinade. It cooks in minutes.

long.t: Bulgogi means "fire meat": thin slices of beef soaked in a sweet, savory marinade, then seared fast over high heat until the edges catch and caramelize. Our version starts with 100% grass-fed ribeye, which is lean and full of flavor, so it soaks up the marinade beautifully.
Why it works

items: Slice it thin: the beef cooks in seconds and stays tender
The grated pear tenderizes the meat and adds natural sweetness
A very hot pan gives you those smoky, charred edges

long.t: The recipe (serves 4 to 6, all organic)

items: ½ small pear, peeled and grated (an apple works too)
¼ cup soy sauce, or coconut aminos
2 tbsp brown sugar, or raw honey
1 tbsp gochujang (Korean red chili paste), to taste
2 tbsp grass-fed ghee or tallow, for the pan

long.t: How to make it

items: Firm up the steak in the freezer for 20 to 30 minutes, then slice it as thin as you can, across the grain.
Whisk the pear, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and gochujang. Toss the beef in it, cover and refrigerate for 2 hours or overnight.
Heat a cast-iron skillet or grill pan until it's smoking hot and add a little ghee.
Cook the beef in small batches, 1 to 2 minutes a side, so it sears instead of steaming.
Finish with green onions and sesame seeds.

How it's made
Beekeepers place their hives on platforms along the river's edge so the bees can gather nectar from the tupelo blossoms. The trees bloom for only about 10 days a year.

The trees grow in a small area, and it takes a lot of effort to produce.

Tupelo honey has a high ratio of fructose to glucose, so it stays liquid much longer than most honey.

long.t: A note from our Guernsey farmer
Greetings from the Guernsey farm in eastern Pennsylvania. Our goal is to produce all-natural, beyond-organic, nutrient-dense dairy.

We milk only Golden Guernsey cows that have been tested for the A2/A2 beta-casein gene. Cows that test A1/A2 or A1/A1, we don't buy: A2/A2 milk is very important to us. The cows are tested by a third party to confirm it.
We're also 100% organic and grass-fed.

products.name: Raw Cultured Guernsey Butter
products.desc: Cream cultured overnight, then churned. Tangy and deeply buttery.

long.t: How we make it

items: We warm raw Guernsey heavy cream to 77°F.
We add MM 100, a live, active culture, and hold the cream at that temperature for 24 hours, in stainless steel only.
The cultured cream then sits in ice water for 12 to 24 hours, until it's cold all the way through.
Once it's thoroughly cold, we churn it into butter.

long.t: The culturing gives it a deeper, slightly tangy flavor, like the butter on an old farmhouse table. Enjoy it on good bread first.
